sections.h2: Selling a Dunwoody house on a short timeline
sections.html:
Usually the quickest path is a cash purchase by a buyer who accepts the house untouched and closes on your schedule. An agent listing and a for-sale-by-owner attempt are the alternatives, and either can bring a better price for a house in good repair.

The mid-2025 estimate is 51,792 residents, only 0.3% above the 51,643 counted for April 2020, so the population is close to flat. Without much vacant land to build on, sales here are mostly resales, and a house with deferred repairs competes against updated ones at the same price.

A cash deal suits an heir, a relocating employee, a landlord with a tenant in place, or anyone unwilling to pay for repairs before listing.

Dunwoody is a high-value city. Five-year figures ending 2024 show a middle home value of $602,900 and a middle household income of $121,903. Rent runs about $1,859. Owners live in 56.2% of homes, and 89.1% of residents had not moved in the past year, so households tend to stay put.

Monthly ownership costs run about $2,675 with a mortgage and $955 without. The average commute is a brief 24.9 minutes, and the city covers 13.03 square miles.

Dunwoody's Code of Ordinances forbids short-term rentals of single-family and multi-family homes. That covers stays under 30 days booked through Vrbo, Airbnb and HomeToGo, and the city enforces the ban when someone complains.

The code also bars party houses, meaning residences used for a commercial party that guests pay to attend. Those events belong at special event facilities with special event permits, and private social gatherings are outside the rule. The city tells residents to call 911 about noise or traffic.

For a seller, that removes nightly-rental investors from the buyer pool. Anyone seeking income is left with long-term leases, so a house with a tenant on a standard lease is pitched that way. If you have been hosting guests by the night, stop before listing and leave that use out of your marketing.

The city sends visitors to the DeKalb County School District, which calls itself the third largest district in Georgia, with more than 90,300 students and 137 schools and centers. Assignment depends on the address, so check the district's tools for your exact street instead of quoting a school from memory.

Buyers also ask about public spaces. The city's site features Dunwoody Village, Brook Run Park, and a sculpture exhibit at the Dunwoody Nature Center at Dunwoody Park. The Dunwoody Preservation Trust, a local nonprofit, runs the historic Donaldson-Bannister Farm as an event venue.

sections.h2: How DeKalb property tax is billed and paid
sections.html:
Because Dunwoody lies in DeKalb County, the county's Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bill. It goes to the person recorded as owner each January 1 and to the present owner if that is someone else. A bill that never shows up still has to be paid.

Current-year payments run August 15 through November 15 in two installments, and the first must be paid before the second. Late amounts draw penalties or interest, and paying only part of a bill is allowed. Receipt by the due date is what counts, and for mailed checks the county reads the USPS postmark.

Paying online by e-check costs nothing extra, while cards carry a percentage fee. Earlier-year balances go to a separate delinquent collections division.

Gather what a buyer and title company will ask for, then check city and county records for anything that could stall the closing:

  • The deed, and any trust or estate papers that show who may sign.
  • Loan payoff statements for every mortgage or lien.
  • The DeKalb tax account showing current installments and any delinquent amount.
  • Permit records from the city's Community Development department, including any open work.
  • Any rental or lease agreements, since Dunwoody does not allow stays under 30 days.

The city runs an online portal for licenses and permits and posts a searchable code of ordinances. If the house has an unpermitted addition or an open complaint, learn that before the buyer's inspector does.

Once you accept an offer, the steps are simple. A title company searches the deed history, your closing attorney prepares the settlement statement, and payoffs for the mortgage and any liens are ordered. Property tax is prorated or assigned in the contract, and Georgia's transfer tax is paid before the deed is recorded.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which are usually the slowest steps. That is why closing dates can be short. A financed buyer adds an inspection, an appraisal and a loan approval, and any of them can reopen the price.

If you rent the house out, give the buyer the lease and deposit details early. If you live there, agree on a handover date and a final walkthrough so nothing is left to argue about on the last day.

Ask the closing attorney for the settlement statement a few days ahead and read every line.

sections.h2: What you give up with a cash bid
sections.html:
Cash brings speed and fewer moving parts, and a listing brings the chance of a higher price. With home values this high, the gap between the two can be wide, so get actual numbers instead of assuming.

Ask every buyer for written terms: closing costs, days to close, any inspection or financing contingency, and the consequence of walking away. Then work out your take-home after the mortgage payoff, tax bills and liens, using figures from your lender and the closing attorney.

Owners who are relocating, settling an estate or racing a deadline tend to prize certainty. Owners with a move-in-ready house and flexible timing usually do better on the open market.

sections.h2: Working from home? Check the business license
sections.html:
The city requires a business license for any business with a physical location inside it. A home-based business should confirm its status with the licensing office before a sale, because a buyer will ask whether any certificate transfers or ends.

The Planning Commission and the city's list of zoning and variance decisions show what is under review. Read them if a rezoning or redevelopment is happening near your street, since buyers sometimes ask.

Share what you know early, and the title and inspection period is less likely to unravel the deal.

faqs.q: Is Airbnb hosting legal in Dunwoody?
faqs.a: No. The city code forbids short-term rentals of houses and multi-family homes, including stays under 30 days booked through Vrbo, Airbnb and similar services, and the city acts on complaints.

faqs.q: Which office collects property tax on a Dunwoody house?
faqs.a: The DeKalb County Tax Commissioner. Current-year payments run August 15 through November 15, with two installments allowed and penalties on late amounts.

faqs.q: What is a typical Dunwoody home worth?
faqs.a: The five-year figures ending 2024 show $602,900 as the middle value of owned homes. That is a citywide number, and no single house is guaranteed to match it.

faqs.q: Which public school system covers Dunwoody?
faqs.a: The DeKalb County School District. Your street address decides which schools your home feeds.

faqs.q: Is selling a Dunwoody house with a tenant allowed?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. A buyer keeping the tenant needs the terms, and one wanting a vacant house will price that in.
